summary: trezor-lib postinstall exfiltrates installer secrets and wallet material to Pipedream webhook
details: The package impersonates the Trezor hardware wallet ecosystem (name 'trezor-lib', description 'Trezor hardware wallet integration library', crypto/wallet keywords) but ships no wallet functionality. Its postinstall.js runs automatically on npm install and reads a hardcoded list of installer-side secret files, including.env*,.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, and ~/.ssh/id_* private keys, then walks the home directory for dotfile entries matching /wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i and reads Solana/Ethereum keystores. It packages up to 8KB slices of each matched file along with os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username and POSTs the collected data over HTTPS to the hardcoded endpoint https://enxhcjpo5ev.x.pipedream.net/c. The network call is wrapped in try/catch to fail silently. There is no first-party purpose served by this behavior; the destination is a third-party webhook that the installer did not opt into.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
